Unlike GMM, HMM adds "memory," allowing it to better reflect how market conditions evolve over time. As a fun historical note, Leonard Baum (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_ E._Baum), one of the first employees of Monemetrics (the precursor to Renaissance Technologies, considered the most successful quantitative hedge fund ever), co-developed the Baum-Welch algorithm. This algorithm, a special case of Expectation-Maximization (EM), is used to estimate the parameters of an HMM. According to Gregory Zuckerman's book (Zuckerman, 2019), The Man Hlho Solved the Market, James Simons, founder of Renaissance Technologies, said about his early days at Monemetrics: "Once I got Lenny (Leonard) involved, I could see the possibilities of building models."
